issues.situation: Bench fixtures (40k/tests/saves/mirror_orks_2000_postdeploy and asym_2000_postdeploy) do not use Orks_2000: they keep the frozen 1.0.19 Speedwaaagh!/Kult of Speed roster (commit 6f07340 'mirrored rather than rebuilt'). Its 4 Stormboyz units per Ork side are the only bench units like the findings, and they carry 'Full Throttle: The unit gains the Advance & Charge ability.' The engine never grants that: the UnitAbilityManager 'Full Throttle' row has condition 'ork11e' and no effects; OrkAbilities11e only offers full_throttle to units that also have Turbo Engine, Shokk Attack Engine or Pulse Jet; and Stormboyz are not SPEED FREEKS, so OrkDetachments11e.advance_allows_charge (Kult of Speed) does not cover them. ChargePhase therefore refuses their charge after an Advance outside the War Cry turn. But _advance_charge_text_is_only_waaagh returns false for them (a non-Waaagh! ability names both words), so the patched gate still Advances every bench Stormboyz ATTACK conversion within 24" (chase cap 26"). That is the exact s7468 failure, left in every Ork bench game. The only bench units the patch changes are the other Waaagh!-only melee seekers: 2 Gretchin hordes (melee-focused only through Runtherd tools S5 A3) and the lone Mek (Killsaw only). There is no measurement for these units, and they now become charge-eligible: against bench targets with 24"+ guns (Custodian Guard, Allarus, Prosecutors, Deffkoptas, Stompa) or CHARACTERs, the scorer adds +2, plus cheap-unit trade efficiency, against the Ork bar (1.0/1.2 before modifiers). So the bench that decides shipping would measure Gretchin/Mek charges at noise level, not the finding. The report's reach ('every Ork COORD-4 attack conversion', counted in an Orks_2000 game) does not carry over to the bench.
issues.proposed_change: In _melee_chase_gate, for units with a Waaagh! ability, stop reading ability text and ask the engine: can_advance_and_charge = flags.effect_advance_and_charge OR EffectPrimitivesData.has_effect_advance_and_charge(unit) (the predicate ChargePhase uses; EffectPrimitivesData is a global class_name the AI already calls) OR the start-of-move rile check in the next issue. Keep the old text fallback only for non-Waaagh! units so the Custodes mirror stays identical. The fix then also fires on the 4 bench Stormboyz units (band 24"), so the bench tests the hypothesis. Add the [WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE] tag to AI_LAB_KEEP_LOG_GREP so the bench reports fires per unit name.

issues.situation: Orks_2000 games: the list behind both findings and the round-4 sweeps, shipped to players (no effect in the bench). The Beastboss leads the Beast Snagga Boyz. The AI always uses Keep Huntin'! (OrkAbilities11e.ai_score 2.5 against the 1.0 bar) in the unit_selected_to_move window, before the Advance roll; the s7473 and s7472 saves log 'AI uses Keep Huntin'! with Beastboss at Beast Snagga Boyz' in rounds 1 and 2. rile_up_diffs then sets effect_advance_and_charge on the whole group, so the base's Advance-to-attack was legal: both positions charged after Advancing, as the report says. This happens after the plan, so at plan time the patch sees no flag and forces a Normal move whenever the target is within move+12" (18" centroid), throwing away the re-rolled D6 (about 4.5") of legal approach. From round 3, or once the unit is below 10 models (then not a horde), conversions reach 20". In the 12-18" band this cuts this round's charge chance for the list's main melee unit (Beastboss A6 S12 AP-2 D2 SH2) from roughly 90%+ to roughly 40-60% (for example, 15" away: about 9" left after a Normal move vs about 4.5" after an Advance). The same blind spot covers Get Back in da Race!, Intimidating Motivation and Kult of Speed SPEED FREEKS, which are detachment checks rather than flags.
issues.proposed_change: Treat the unit as able to advance-and-charge when the engine predicate above says so OR its own attached group holds a start-of-move rile ability that will target it: OrkAbilities11e.group_has(uid, 'keep_huntin') with the BEAST SNAGGA keyword, 'get_back_in_da_race' with SPEED FREEKS, or 'intimidating_motivation' with ORKS, AND not OrkAbilities11e.army_used_this_round(player, slug). The module is already lazily loaded as _ork_abilities_module. Add a test: an attached Keep Huntin'! holder with an unused round keeps the Advance; once the round's use is spent, it makes a Normal move.

issues.situation: Measured positions: the patch changes the AI's action at all four measured Ork 'advances to attack' positions. These include s7418 r3 P2 Stormboyz -> Blade Champion Gamma (8.8"; not riled, P2's War Cry already used), which is class HARMFUL: the AI's own Advance-to-attack beat holding obj_center by -8.33 [-12.33, -4.34] (n12; case 40k/tests/rollout_cases/s1d/20261030_014824_sweep2_07__s7418_r3_p2_movement_1_4.json). The report's guardrail checks omit it. All four measured alternatives were 'objective instead of attack'; none measures 'Normal move + charge' against 'Advance'. The report concedes that s7473's +10 came from not charging, and its only s7468 replay scored the fix 1.0 vs base 12.0 (one seed).
issues.proposed_change: Before the bench, replay s7468, s7473, s7472 and s7418 with FIX_WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE=1 vs 0 over at least 12 paired seeds (the patched action as branch B). Add s7418 as a guardrail: the fix must not score below the base there.

issues.situation: Full-game horizon. When the charge after the move is declined or fails (frequent at the far edge of the band, where 9-12" charges succeed 3-28% of the time), the chaser ends about 3.5-4.5" behind where the base Advance would have put it. One-round rollouts do not price this for later-round positioning cards (Behind Enemy Lines, Engage on All Fronts, Centre Ground). The units the patch changes in the bench have their own later-round cost: Gretchin (OC 2 per model, the list's objective holders) and the lone Mek (a CHARACTER, Assassination VP) gain charges the scorer may take, and can die a half-turn earlier, which can cost primary VP in rounds 4-5. This is the round-2 failure mode (units held back scored less).
issues.proposed_change: Optional refinement: switch to a Normal move only when the charge after it is reasonably likely (closest-model distance after the move <= ~9", about 28%+), otherwise keep the Advance. Judge the revised fix on full-game bench VP split by primary and secondary (per_card), not on rollouts.

reviews.fires_in_bench: Low, and on units unrelated to the findings. Custodes mirror: 0 fires (no unit has Waaagh!), so every pair is identical. Custodes vs Orks: 0 in the half of the games where the candidate plays Custodes (identical games). In the games where the candidate plays Orks, about 0-2 fires per game (best guess about 1), mostly in rounds 3-5, outside the War Cry turn (round 1 or 2). Orks mirror: the same rate per game (only the candidate's seat). Only 3 bench units per Ork side can fire: the 2 Gretchin hordes and the lone Mek, the only melee seekers whose sole advance+charge text is Waaagh!. Gretchin hordes convert to ATTACK only within 12" in rounds 1-2 (Ork aggression 1.2 < 1.5) or within the 10-12" hold limits. The 4 Stormboyz units, the only bench analogue of the findings, never fire: their frozen 'Full Throttle' text makes the helper return false, although the engine does not let them charge after advancing. The designer's '2 fires in a full game' came from an Orks_2000 game (s7438) and does not carry over. With the proposed engine-based predicate, the Stormboyz would add several fires per candidate-Ork game. Not verified with logs: no bench-roster game logs are on this machine, and bench_results files drop COORD-4 lines.
reviews.strengths: The rules diagnosis is correct: the gate's text test reads the conditional Waaagh! rule as a standing advance-and-charge grant, while the game marks riling with flags.effect_advance_and_charge and ChargePhase refuses the charge without it. The patch keeps the flag check first, so the War Cry turn and Zodgrod's permanently flagged Gretchin still Advance. It is a tiny change at one decision point, behind a switch (FIX_WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE, 0 = base), with a log tag when it changes a decision and a failing-first test with sensible guards (riled up, another ability, out of reach, param 0). It does not touch AI-GAP-4 or RACE-1, so the Lootas guardrails (including the harmful s7470 -5.50) are unchanged. It does not change WHO chases (pass-2.5 conversions and OC re-opening/backfill are identical), has no keeper/earmark/FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE dependency, and never fires for Custodes. The report is honest that s7473's gain came from not charging and names the Keep Huntin'! risk.
reviews.summary: The idea (a chaser that cannot charge after Advancing should make a Normal move when that reaches charge range) is sound. The predicate is wrong because it decides from ability text, not from what the engine grants. In the bench fixtures (frozen Speedwaaagh!/Kult of Speed roster), the 4 Stormboyz units, the only analogue of the findings, carry an unimplemented 'Full Throttle: gains the Advance & Charge ability' text, so the helper returns false and they keep the exact s7468 bug. The patch instead fires only for 2 Gretchin hordes and a lone Mek, units with no evidence, so the shipping bench would measure noise rather than the finding. In Orks_2000 games, it misreads Keep Huntin'!, which the AI uses every round at the start of the move and which makes the Advance legal for the Beastboss-led Beast Snagga Boyz. The patch discards that legal Advance distance, cutting their charge odds in the 12-18" band. It also changes the harmful-class s7418 Stormboyz position without checking it, and none of the four measured Ork attack positions measures the patch's own action (Normal move + charge). Revise: for Waaagh! units use EffectPrimitivesData.has_effect_advance_and_charge(unit) plus a start-of-move rile check (OrkAbilities11e.group_has + army_used_this_round); keep the text fallback only for non-Ork units; replay s7468, s7473, s7472 and s7418 with the fix on vs off over at least 12 seeds; and count [WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE] in bench logs. Patch: /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/tools/ai_lab/r4_designs/waaagh_advance_charge/narrow.patch.

issues.situation: Orks_2000 Beast Snagga Boyz led by an attached Beastboss: the unit of finding s7473 and guardrail s7472, the two other decisions the patch changes in its own checks. At plan time flags.effect_advance_and_charge is false, because the riled-up state from Keep Huntin'! ends at the start of the Ork turn. So the gate sets attack_advance=false and logs 'not riled up, an Advance would forfeit the charge'. That claim is wrong. BEGIN_ADVANCE and BEGIN_NORMAL_MOVE both open the unit_selected_to_move window (MovementPhase ~1212). There the AI always uses Keep Huntin'! (OrkAbilities11e.ai_score = 2.5; once per round; the unit's own group is a valid target), and rile_up_diffs sets effect_advance_and_charge. So the base Advance kept the charge. Base record reinforce_cap_base_f2/A_5001 shows it: 'Beast Snagga Boyz advances to attack Burna Boyz Beta (9.3")' -> 'AI uses Keep Huntin'!' -> charge at 2.2" (97%), rolled 3. With the patch the unit makes a Normal move to 3.3" (92%). At 14" the charge chance falls from about 72% (the AI plans M+2) to about 42% (8" gap). The same false negative applies to Get Back in da Race! and Intimidating Motivation, and to selection-window stratagems such as DAT ONE'S EVEN BIGGA!.
issues.proposed_change: Before clearing the flag, keep the Advance when the unit's group can be riled up when it is selected to move. That holds when the unit, or an alive attached character (snapshot.units[id] for each id in attachment_data.attached_characters), has Keep Huntin'! (unit is BEAST SNAGGA), Get Back in da Race! (SPEED FREEKS) or Intimidating Motivation (ORKS). Optionally also require not army_used_this_round(player, slug), using the OrkAbilities11e module the AI already loads (_ork_abilities_module). Add a test: Beast Snagga Boyz with an attached Beastboss (Keep Huntin'!) 12" from the enemy, fix on -> BEGIN_ADVANCE.

issues.situation: The benchmark Ork roster is mirror_orks_2000_postdeploy / asym_2000_postdeploy (Kult of Speed, 40kdc-data 1.0.19), not Orks_2000.json. In it, all 4 Stormboyz units per side carry 'Waaagh!' plus 'Full Throttle: The unit gains the Advance & Charge ability.' _advance_charge_text_is_only_waaagh returns false on Full Throttle, so the base Advance stays. The engine does not implement that text: the UnitAbilityManager 'Full Throttle' row has no effects, OrkAbilities11e full_throttle needs turbo_engine/shokk_attack_engine/pulse_jet, and EffectPrimitives gives Kult of Speed advance-and-charge only to SPEED FREEKS. So these Stormboyz still Advance and cannot charge. That is the exact bug of the confirmed s7468 finding, and the fix never fires on them in the bench. It fires only on the bench Gretchin and the Mek, which have no measured position. The exemption reads ability text again, which is the same misread the cluster is about.
issues.proposed_change: For units that carry Waaagh!, with the fix on, ignore all ability text. Treat the unit as able to advance and charge only when one of these holds: flags.effect_advance_and_charge; EffectPrimitivesData.has_effect_advance_and_charge(unit), which covers detachment and codex grants such as Kult of Speed SPEED FREEKS; or the selection-time riling from the first issue. Keep Custodes and other factions out of scope (the Waaagh! requirement stays). Add a test with the 1.0.19 Stormboyz abilities (Waaagh! + Full Throttle) 12" from the enemy, fix on -> BEGIN_NORMAL_MOVE. It fails on the current patch. Re-run the guardrails and recount bench fires.

issues.situation: test_other_advance_charge_ability_still_advances uses the real Swift Onslaught text and asserts that the unit Advances, as if Swift Onslaught kept a real advance-and-charge. In this engine Swift Onslaught is re-rolls only (UnitAbilityManager row effects []; CustodesAbilities.advance_allows_charge only for the Dropship flag). So the test pins the base misread as expected behaviour. The Custodes-mirror bench log shows that misread: 'Blade Champion Gamma advances to attack Allarus Custodians #3 (6.6" away — closing to charge range (0.6" after move))'.
issues.proposed_change: Rename the test and its comment to a scope check ('units without Waaagh! are unchanged by this fix'), not a claim that the ability is advance-and-charge. Or rewrite it once the exemption is engine-based.

issues.situation: The report overstates or misstates some checks. It counts 'decisions_changed 2/2', but only s7468 matches the alternative's intent. The s7473 gain (stay on obj_center, do not charge) is not addressed, and the s7473 change is the Keep Huntin'! case. The s7442 explanation is wrong: base says '6.7" after move', so a Normal move does reach charge range; the decision is unchanged because the Terminator Assault Squad's matching ability is not Waaagh!. Guardrail s7470 (added later) is missing; by code it is unchanged, because Lootas are not melee seekers and AI-GAP-4/RACE-1 are untouched. The '2 fires per full game' came from the Orks_2000 roster, not the benchmark roster. The 1-seed values (s7468 fix 1.0 vs base 12.0) are noise.
issues.proposed_change: Correct the s7442 note, add s7470 as 'unchanged (not a melee seeker)', report the matched-intent count as 1/2, and state the bench-roster firing separately.

issues.situation: The generic threshold makes a Normal move whenever the gap after it is 12" or less. At 11-12" gaps that trades the Advance for a 2.8-8% charge, and M12 Stormboyz trigger it for any enemy within 24". The designer lists this as risk (1).
issues.proposed_change: Optionally require a charge chance worth the lost distance (for example, a gap of 9" or less after the Normal move) for the Waaagh! case only. Otherwise watch it in the bench.

issues.situation: _melee_chase_gate is also called as a probe by the V9R keeper-release revision (kr_gate). With FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE on, the [WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE] line would print for moves that are never made, which inflates the bench 'fires' count. It is off in V9R, so the bench is not affected now.
issues.proposed_change: Log at ATTACK execution (where attack_advance is consumed), or tag the line as a plan decision so probe calls can be told apart.

issues.situation: test_ork_chaser_out_of_reach_still_advances puts the enemy exactly on the chase cap: 20.0" == max(MELEE_AGGRESSION_ADVANCE_THRESHOLD_INCHES=20, M6+14). A float difference or a constant change turns it into a CHASE-CAP skip, and the test fails for an unrelated reason.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
Estimated from the trigger conditions and the fixture rosters; not run. Trigger: an Ork melee seeker carrying Waaagh!, whose only ability naming both advance and charge is Waaagh!, converted to ATTACK with the enemy within M+12", while flags.effect_advance_and_charge is false (no War Cry that turn).
(1) Custodes mirror: never fires (no unit has Waaagh!), so all pairs are identical.
(2) Orks mirror (mirror_orks_2000_postdeploy, Kult of Speed, 1.0.19 data). The 4 Stormboyz units per side never fire, because their 'Full Throttle ... Advance & Charge' text makes the helper return false. Warbikers, Deffkoptas, Deffkilla Wartrikes, Wazdakka and the Stompa are not melee seekers (strong ranged weapons). Only the 2 Gretchin units (Runtherd tools S5 makes them melee seekers) and the lone Mek (Killsaw only) can fire. Gretchin holding a home objective chase only enemies within 10-12" (FACTION_AGGRESSION_ORKS = 1.2), so every Gretchin chase fires. Rough estimate: 0-2 fires per game for the candidate's Ork side, often 0.
(3) Custodes vs Orks (asym_2000_postdeploy, Orks = P2): the same units, and only in the games where the candidate plays P2, so at least half the games are identical.
The bench therefore cannot show the Stormboyz gain the cluster measured (s7468). It would measure only Gretchin/Mek chase changes, which have no measured position. The designer's '2 fires per full game' were Stormboyz on the Orks_2000 roster (s7438), which is not the bench roster.
reviews.strengths:
- Small and readable: one extra condition at the right place (the ATTACK Advance/Normal decision in _melee_chase_gate, used once per unit per plan, so no hot-loop cost).
- Param 0 restores the base exactly. The only ungated effect is one get_param read noted in _param_reads.
- The [WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE] log line fires exactly when a decision changes. No debug log was removed, and the style and tags match the file.
- The helper is null-safe for String and Dictionary abilities.
- The patch applies cleanly on 5e70bc2 and on top of keeper_release_rev_vs_v9.patch (checked in scratch). It does not depend on FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE.
- Correct for the confirmed s7468 case: on Orks_2000 Stormboyz the Prosecutors sit on obj_nml_1, so a Normal move toward them is close to the measured alternative.
- Ork shooting units (Lootas, etc.) are untouched: AI-GAP-4/RACE-1 are not changed, so the harmful-alternative guardrail s7470 and the Lootas guardrails are safe by code.
- The test pins the fix on and erases the override. It drives _decide_movement (the real plan -> chase gate -> ATTACK execution path) and fails on base for the right reason (base Advances because of the Waaagh! text).
- The report is candid that the s7473 intent is not matched and that Keep Huntin'! is a risk.
reviews.summary:
Revise: the code is clean, but the check that decides 'can this unit charge after Advancing' is still based on ability text, and in the data the game uses it is wrong in both directions.

What works: the patch is correctly gated (param 0 = base), costs almost nothing, logs only when a decision changes, and its test drives the real decision path and fails on base for the right reason. It fixes the measured s7468 Stormboyz case on the Orks_2000 roster.

Problem 1 (fires where it should not): it forces a Normal move on Beastboss-led Beast Snagga Boyz. Keep Huntin'! riles that unit up when it is selected to move, so the Advance never cost it the charge. A base record shows the Advance, then Keep Huntin'!, then a 97% charge. This case is 2 of the 3 decisions the patch changes in its own checks, and the log line wrongly says the Advance would forfeit the charge.

Problem 2 (does not fire where it should): its exemption trusts the 1.0.19 'Full Throttle: gains the Advance & Charge ability' text, which the engine does not implement. So the benchmark's 4 Stormboyz units per side keep the exact bug. In the bench the fix fires only on Gretchin and the Mek (roughly 0-2 times per Ork game, never in the Custodes mirror), which have no measured position. The bench cannot show the gain the cluster measured.

Concrete revision: for Waaagh! units, decide from what the engine actually grants. That means the flag, EffectPrimitives.has_effect_advance_and_charge, or a riling ability in the unit's attached group (Keep Huntin'!, Get Back in da Race!, Intimidating Motivation) that is unused this round; ignore all other text. Add tests for the attached-Beastboss case (expect Advance) and for 1.0.19 Stormboyz (expect Normal move).

issues.situation: The report says the fix fires in 'every Ork (and SW) game' but does not mention the Custodes mirror. In the frozen bench Custodes roster (mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy and asym_2000_postdeploy, Lions of the Emperor), every Blade Champion has 'Martial Inspiration: Once per battle, the unit gains the Advance & Charge ability.' The old text test matches it. The engine does not implement it: it is not in UnitAbilityManager.ABILITY_EFFECTS, and CustodesAbilities/CustodesEnhancements grant advance-and-charge only through the Dropship or Sally Forth flags. The bench Blade Champions are unattached, melee-only melee seekers (3 per side). In the bench records on disk (bench_data/ai_versions_*), 'Blade Champion advances to attack ... closing to charge range' happens 5.6-6.5 times per Custodes-mirror game across 465 V0-V5-era games, and about once per game in the three V9-era games (/tmp/v9check, scratchpad firetest_season). This fix turns every one of those into a Normal move plus a possible charge. That is the largest change in the fixture where round 2 lost 6.26 VP per game, and no measured position covers it.
issues.proposed_change: No code change needed. Before shipping, run one rollout of a Blade Champion attack-Advance from the Custodes mirror (for example V9 seed 96021, round 4, P2: 'Blade Champion Gamma advances to attack Allarus Custodians #3, 0.6" after move'). Also make the judge read the Custodes-mirror bench E separately instead of only the pooled E.

issues.situation: The long-trip part (_should_unit_advance_long_trip) is wider than the evidence. Both confirmed findings are chase-gate decisions. The long-trip change now blocks the long-trip Advance of any text-matched unit when any enemy is within M+12", including units whose charge does not matter. Examples: Orks_2000 shooting units (Lootas, Burna Boyz, Tankbustas, Battlewagons). In s7436 r3 this part alone moves Lootas Beta (Allarus 14.5" away) from 'Advance to flip obj_nml_1' to a Normal move to obj_center, close to the measured alternative, which leans negative (-5.25 [-17.5, 7.0], neutral). It also hits bench Gretchin hordes in rounds 1-2 when the nearest enemy is 12-18" away: there the chase gate itself returns OBJ-PRIORITY because Ork aggression is 1.2 < 1.5, yet they lose an objective Advance (22 OC per unit in the bench) to keep a charge the AI has decided not to make. Bench impact is small: from the start positions this window is rare, and bench melee seekers within M+12 are converted to ATTACK by the gate anyway (chase cap 20" or 26" is wider than M+12).
issues.proposed_change: Apply the new long-trip enemy check only to units for which keeping the charge matters. In _should_unit_advance_long_trip, when FIX_WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE is on and the unit's text matched, run the M+12 block only if _is_melee_seeker(unit) is true and the unit is not a horde in rounds <=2 with the nearest enemy beyond 12". Otherwise keep the old skip. The alternative is to leave this call site on the old estimate. Neither option changes bench behaviour or the two findings, and both remove the s7436 cascade.

issues.situation: The chase gate now picks a Normal move whenever (centroid gap minus M) <= 12". In the historical flipped decisions, 20% end 9-12" from the target (2D6 charge odds about 3-28%) and another 20% end 6-9" away. The charge evaluator is permissive: the threshold is about 1.0 on a probability-scaled score, CHARGE_RETALIATION_WEIGHT is 0.5, and the minimum probability is 3%. In the V9 game a lone Blade Champion declared a 17% charge into Custodian Guard, which then hit back for 13.9 expected damage against 6 W. So this fix routes more low-odds, high-retaliation charges by lone characters (Blade Champion, Mek) and Gretchin through that evaluator. Today the unit Advances adjacent and the enemy charges it on 27% of these flips. The net sign is unclear.
issues.proposed_change: Optional refinement: in _melee_chase_gate, keep the Advance when the post-move gap is above about 9" (charge chance below about 28%), because the charge is unlikely anyway and the Advance sets up next turn. The cleaner option is to ask the charge evaluator for the EV, including retaliation, before choosing the Normal move. Measure it as a separate parameter.

issues.situation: In Orks_2000 games, Keep Huntin'! (Beastboss to BEAST SNAGGA), Get Back in da Race! (Wartrike to SPEED FREEKS) and Intimidating Motivation rile a unit at the unit_selected_to_move window, after the plan. That sets effect_advance_and_charge, so an Advance-to-attack can be legal. The fix cannot see this pending rile-up and plans a Normal move. The cost is small: the gate only flips when a Normal move already reaches charge range, so only the charge is about 3.5" longer. These abilities are not in the frozen Kult of Speed bench roster, and Turbo Engine / Full Throttle sets its flag in the Command phase, which the plan can see. The report does not mention this case.
issues.proposed_change: Document it. If wanted, treat an unused rile-up source of this kind (once per battle round, within 6" of a BEAST SNAGGA or SPEED FREEKS unit) as advance-and-charge for that unit's gate decision only.

issues.situation: s7473 (+10.03 over 36 seeds) only partly matches. The measured better option was 'Normal move onto obj_center'. The fix produces 'Normal move to attack Allarus (3.5" after move)', which keeps the attack conversion. Part of the measured gain may come from staying on obj_center, which this design does not capture. The designer's 1-seed check (5 to 21) is weak evidence.
issues.proposed_change: No change in this cluster. Note that the hold-versus-attack part of s7473 is still open.

reviews.fires_in_bench: It fires in all 3 fixtures, often, so the bench can measure it (unlike V9's keeper fix). Custodes mirror: Blade Champions (3 per side, text match through 'Martial Inspiration', engine says no). Historical bench records show 5.6-6.5 flipped 'advance to attack, closing to charge range' moves per game, counting both seats, over 465 V0-V5-era games, and about 1 per game in the three V9-era games. That gives about 0.5-3 flipped moves per game in the candidate seat. Distribution of flips: 35% end within 3\" of the target, 25% at 3-6\", 20% at 6-9\", 20% at 9-12\". Orks mirror (Kult of Speed frozen roster): 4 Stormboyz per seat (M12, nearest enemy within 24\", 'Full Throttle' text not granted by the engine), plus 2 Gretchin and 1 Mek when the gate converts them to attack, plus the Stompa in its gap 10-12\" _should_unit_advance window. Estimate: about 3-8 changed moves per game per candidate seat outside the one Waaagh! turn. This is from roster and code analysis; there are no Orks-fixture records on disk to count. Speed Freeks (Wartrikes, Warbikers, Deffkoptas, Wazdakka) do not change, because Kult of Speed Adrenaline Junkies is inside has_effect_advance_and_charge. Asym: fires in both games of each pair (Blade Champions on the Custodes seat; Stormboyz, Gretchin, Mek and Stompa on the Ork seat). The long-trip and _should_unit_advance changes produce many log lines but rarely change a final bench move, because bench melee seekers near enemies are converted by the gate.
reviews.strengths: The root cause is correct and checked against the engine. ChargePhase allows a charge after an Advance only through EffectPrimitivesData.has_effect_advance_and_charge. In 11e, FactionAbilityManager.unit_has_adrenaline_junkies returns false, and Kult of Speed Speed Freeks are covered by OrkDetachments11e.advance_allows_charge. The Waaagh! and rile_up_diffs, Turbo Engine, SW doctrines and Custodes Sally Forth, Dropship and stratagem grants all set the flag or are inside the predicate. So the AI now asks exactly the question the engine enforces. The change is small and covered by one parameter (off restores the exact base), and it fixes all three AI consumers of the misread (get_unit_ability_profile is unused). It leaves the advance-and-shoot text test alone, which protects the Lootas guardrails. Both confirmed findings flip in the measured direction for the move mode. On s7418 (harmful alternative = hold) the attack is kept and gains a legal charge. The harmful-class Ork Advances s7403, s7407, s7417, s7425, s7468 r1 and s7470 are unchanged (no enemy within M+12), and s7423 is unchanged (Waaagh! flag set). reviews.summary: Sound root-cause design with no major game-impact problem found in the bench. In the bench rosters the misread makes Kult of Speed Stormboyz, Gretchin, Mek and Custodes Blade Champions Advance 'to attack' and then fail to charge in every turn except the Waaagh! turn. The fix replaces those moves with Normal moves that keep the charge. It does not change hold-versus-attack decisions, Speed Freeks, or the Waaagh! turn. In this game's scoring (objective holding plus destroyed-unit secondaries), extra charges that strike first should help, and the base behaviour (stand next to the enemy without charging, and get charged first 27% of the time) is the worst of both options. Concerns are all minor. (1) The report misses that the fix fires in the Custodes mirror through Blade Champions ('Martial Inspiration' text, not implemented in the engine): historically 1-6 flips per game, with no measured position. Check that fixture's E separately before shipping. (2) The long-trip part is wider than the evidence and alone causes the s7436 cascade in Orks_2000. Limiting it to melee seekers costs nothing in the bench. (3) The gate threshold sends some units into charges that need 9-12\", through a charge evaluator that underweights retaliation. (4) Rile-ups at unit_selected_to_move in Orks_2000 are not visible to the plan. reviews.summary:
I read the code and the saved positions (no Godot run, as instructed). The design is sound for units that cannot rile up, and that includes every bench unit it touches. It needs one revision: it ignores units that are riled when selected to move.

The predicate is read at plan time. Keep Huntin'!, Intimidating Motivation and Get Back in da Race! fire inside BEGIN_ADVANCE, after the mode is chosen, and the AI always takes them. The base save of finding #2 (s7473) shows the Beast Snagga Boyz were riled by Keep Huntin'! after their Advance and still charged at 97%. So that finding is not a lost charge: its +10 comes from holding obj_center, which this design does not produce. For BSB+Beastboss the fix also swaps a legal Advance-then-charge for a weaker Normal-move charge.

The concrete change is to add an 'unused rile ability held by the unit's own Attached unit' term to _unit_can_charge_after_advance, with a test.

Smaller points:
- Add tests for the Kult of Speed true-path, for _should_unit_advance, and at planner level.
- Make the _should_unit_advance log print only when the result changes.
- Replay the s7418 guardrail, which the fix changes and nobody measured.
- The report should say the fix fires in all 3 bench fixtures, including the Custodes mirror through Blade Champion 'Martial Inspiration'.

Param 0 restores the base exactly. The design does not depend on the keeper release and applies to V9R.

issues.situation: Riling that happens after the plan is invisible to the check, so the design misdiagnoses its strongest finding. In Orks_2000 games the Beastboss is attached to the Beast Snagga Boyz (BSB). This is true in s7473, s7472 and in P2's army in s7418. The engine offers Keep Huntin'! in the unit_selected_to_move window for both Normal and Advance moves (OrkAbilities11e.WINDOW_ABILITIES). The AI always takes it (ai_score 2.5 against the 1.0 ability threshold). rile_up_diffs sets effect_advance_and_charge and waaagh_active on the group, so the Shooting-phase wipe keeps the flag until the Charge phase. The saves show the ability used every round (players.1.ork11e_ab_uses.keep_huntin = {battle: 2, round: 2} at the round-3 decisions in s7473 and s7472) and free again in round 3. So at s7473 and s7472 the base Advance kept the charge. The report's root cause ('A conceded after its Advance left it unable to charge') is wrong, and its 4-seed +16.75 cannot come from keeping the charge. The measured +10.03 came from not attacking and staying on obj_center. With the patch, has_effect_advance_and_charge is false at plan time because the rile comes later. Every BSB chase within M+12" outside the War Cry turn then becomes a Normal move that gives up the D6" Advance. Example: an enemy 15" away leaves a 9" charge (28%) instead of about 5.5" (72%). In the bench records about a third of chases have a gap of 6" or more after the move, where this matters. The log line also falsely says 'an Advance would forfeit the charge'. This never occurs in the bench (the frozen Kult of Speed list has no riling ability), so the bench cannot catch the regression.

For each pair (keep_huntin, BEAST SNAGGA), (intimidating_motivation, ORKS), (get_back_in_da_race, SPEED FREEKS), check all of: OrkAbilities11e.group_holder(unit_id, slug) != "" (the holder is in the unit's own attached group), the unit has the keyword, and not OrkAbilities11e.army_used_this_round(player, slug). The patch flips all of these. When eligible, the charge AI does declare lone-Blade-Champion charges into Custodian Guard (17-42% odds, 4.2 expected damage against 20 HP), and Custodian Guard retaliation kills a lone Blade Champion. 11e Assassination scores at the end of either turn (5 VP once all CHARACTERs are dead). Each side's War Cry turn is exempt; the AI calls it in R1 if any unit is within 22\", otherwise R2. So flips happen in rounds 2/3-5. SPEED FREEKS units are unaffected: Kult of Speed Adrenaline Junkies is visible at plan time, and the classifier does not count them as melee seekers.
- **Custodes vs Orks: estimated 5-10 per game.** 3 lone Blade Champions on P1 plus 4 Stormboyz on P2.

reviews.strengths:
- **Small surface:** one gate and one parameter; setting it to 0 restores base exactly.
- **Uses the engine's own test:** the same has_effect_advance_and_charge call ChargePhase uses. In the bench rosters the plan-time answer matches the Charge phase exactly; I found no grant there that arrives after the plan. It is correct for every faction whose rule text names a conditional advance-and-charge (Waaagh!, Full Throttle, Martial Inspiration, Space Wolves Combat Doctrines), and it adapts automatically if the engine later implements those grants.
- **Legitimate grants keep Advancing:** an active Waaagh!/War Cry, Adrenaline Junkies, Super Runts' permanent rile and Assault Doctrine are all visible at plan time.
- **Racing is untouched:** RACE-1 and AI-GAP-4 are unchanged, so round-1 objective racing and the s7470/s7436/s7437/s7438 guardrails do not move.
- **No dependency on other fixes:** independent of the keeper release and the other FIX_ params.
- **Positionally safe:** a Normal move is never positionally worse than the Advance when the post-move gap is ≤ about 3\" (a third of bench cases). In the other cases, base units could never charge at all: they Advanced every turn and were themselves charged 57% of the time. So in the bench it is a real rules alignment that turns about 6 or more wasted attack moves per game into charge options.
reviews.summary:
The idea is sound: ask the engine, not the ability text, whether a unit may charge after Advancing. In the three bench rosters the answer at plan time matches what the Charge phase will allow. I verified the engine path (ChargePhase.gd lines 2019 and 2041, EffectPrimitives.gd line 836) and the bench rosters from the decoded saves.

Two problems:

1. **Major: the design misreads its own key finding.** At s7473 (and s7472) the Beast Snagga Boyz have an attached Beastboss. Keep Huntin'! fires when they are selected to move, every round (the saves show it used in rounds 1-2 and free in round 3). It sets effect_advance_and_charge, so the base Advance was legal and kept the charge. The patch checks before that rile, so it turns every Orks_2000 Beast Snagga chase within 18\" outside the War Cry turn into a Normal move and gives up D6\" of charge reach. That is a regression in every Orks_2000 game that the bench cannot see. The fix is small: treat a unit whose attached group holds an unused rile ability (Keep Huntin'!, Intimidating Motivation, Get Back in da Race!, with the matching keyword) as able to advance and charge, and add a test.

2. **Minor: the report's firing claim is wrong for the bench.** It says the patch rarely fires and never for non-Ork units. In fact it fires about 6 times per game in the Custodes mirror (lone Blade Champions' 'Martial Inspiration' text; 90 cases in 15 recorded bench games) and often in both Ork fixtures (Stormboyz' 'Full Throttle'). No measured position covers either unit type. The direction is plausibly positive: these units now charge instead of standing next to the enemy and being charged first, which happened 57% of the time. But lone Blade Champions trading themselves into Custodian Guard, and the Assassination timing that follows, are unmeasured in the fixture that cost 6.26 VP in round 2.

Other gaps: the evidence at s7468 is 4 noisy seeds for a different action than the measured alternative, and the harmful guardrail s7418 changes but was not checked.

Verdict: revise. Add the rile-at-selection check, then measure the Custodes-mirror Blade Champion positions before shipping.

But MovementPhase opens the unit_selected_to_move window for BEGIN_ADVANCE (line 1212) and BEGIN_NORMAL_MOVE (line 1124) alike, and the AI always uses Keep Huntin'! there (OrkAbilities11e.ai_score 2.5). rile_up_diffs sets waaagh_active and effect_advance_and_charge, which survive the Shooting-phase wipe. So the base Advance was charge-legal. The same unit proved it in round 2 of the s7473 game: BEGIN_ADVANCE, then 'AI uses Keep Huntin'! with Beastboss at Beast Snagga Boyz', then DECLARE_CHARGE (83%), then charged. reviews.fires_in_bench: These are estimates from the code's trigger conditions; I did not run any games. A flip needs: a melee seeker whose ability text has 'advance' and 'charge'; no engine grant; an attack conversion in the chase gate; and the enemy within M+12 inches (cap max(20, M+14)). By fixture: (1) Orks mirror (frozen Kult of Speed list): per side, 4 Stormboyz (M12, flip whenever the enemy is within 24 inches), the Mek and 2 Gretchin qualify. SPEED FREEKS units (Warbikers, Wartrikes, Deffkoptas, Wazdakka) get a real Kult of Speed grant and never flip. No flips during the War Cry round. Expect several flips per game (roughly 2-8) from round 1-2 on, so most pairs should diverge. (2) Custodes vs Orks: P2's same Ork units, plus rarely P1's unattached Blade Champions ('Martial Inspiration' text, not implemented in 11e). Roughly 1-5 per game; most pairs diverge. (3) Custodes mirror: only the 3 unattached Blade Champions per side can flip, and only when converted to attack within 18 inches. The one local replay with the bench game id (c02b1ee3, 5 rounds) had zero Blade Champion attack conversions. They moved via the PHASE-PLAN charge-intent Normal-move path, and the 6 'advances to attack' were Custodian Guard at 18.1-19.8 inches, which the fix does not change. So about 0-1 per game, mostly identical pairs. Keep Huntin'!, Intimidating Motivation and Get Back in da Race! do not exist in the bench rosters, so the bench cannot reveal the major issue. The report's '<1 fire per Ork game' comes from Orks_2000 replays and understates bench firing.
reviews.strengths: The change is small and fully gated: FIX_WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE=0 skips the only new block, so base behaviour is exact, and the patch applies cleanly to c4b8d98. It asks the same predicate ChargePhase uses (has_effect_advance_and_charge, ChargePhase.gd 2040-2041), so the AI and the engine agree on the Waaagh!, Kult of Speed SPEED FREEKS, Turbo Engine, Sally Forth and cus11e grants. It also handles the frozen bench texts (Full Throttle, Martial Inspiration) and the 11e 'Swift Onslaught', which is re-rolls only and which the cluster hint misread. The race paths (AI-GAP-4, RACE-1) are untouched, so every race-Advance guardrail is unchanged (s7470, s7436, s7437, s7438 x2). There is no null risk: flags are read with .get, and units with an empty snapshot are skipped upstream. Cost is negligible: one call site per plan, and it runs only when the text test is true. No log is removed, and the new [WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE] print fires exactly when the decision flips. The test pins the override on, erases it afterwards, fails on base for the right reason (dormant Waaagh! means base Advances), and checks that param 0 restores the old behaviour. s7468 (Stormboyz, Waaagh! spent, no rile source) is a real lost-charge case, and the fix handles it as intended. The risk section is honest about long-shot charges.
reviews.summary: The idea is sound: ask the rules engine, not ability text, whether a unit may charge after Advancing. The gating, cost, logging and engine parity are all correct. But the check runs at plan time, while Codex: Orks (11e) Keep Huntin'!, Intimidating Motivation and Get Back in da Race! rile the unit in its unit_selected_to_move window afterwards, and the AI always uses them. For the Orks_2000 Beast Snagga Boyz plus Beastboss, the base Advance was charge-legal in s7473 and s7472 (Keep Huntin'! free in round 3; the same unit Advanced, was riled and charged in round 2). There the fix only throws away 3.5-4.5 inches of charge reach. It also means s7473's measured gain is not the 'lost charge' the report claims, since the fix still leaves obj_center to charge. Revise: count an unused own-group rile ability as an engine grant (OrkAbilities11e.group_holder + group_has_keyword + army_used_this_round), add a Keep Huntin'! test, and re-measure s7473/s7472/s7418. In the bench the fix will fire often through the frozen Kult of Speed Stormboyz, Mek and Gretchin, rarely through Custodes Blade Champions, and almost never in the Custodes mirror. The report's firing estimate does not reflect those rosters. The Lootas race guardrails, including harmful s7470, cannot move because AI-GAP-4 and RACE-1 are untouched. This is the most general design: one engine-predicate helper used at all three places that read the text, param 0 restores the base exactly, and it fires in every fixture. But the RACE-1 and AI-GAP-4 changes go past the evidence. Any unit whose text matches but has no engine grant loses long-trip Advances whenever an enemy is within M+12". That hits Orks_2000 Lootas, Burna Boyz and Tankbustas in rounds 2-3; their 'Dat's Our Loot!' and similar texts pass the advance+shoot check that is now skipped. It caused the s7436 cascade toward the neutral alternative that leans negative, and it hits the bench Gretchin hordes. This is the round-2 hold-back failure mode, and it is unmeasured. The design misses Keep Huntin'!. Its AI-GAP-4 log line prints even when the function then Advances anyway. The tests call the functions directly and have no case where the engine says yes and no AI-GAP-4 case. The const comment cites the old 12-seed number.

The diagnosis is correct, the change is the smallest, and the test is the best of the three: it drives _decide_movement and fails on base. The report is honest that s7473 is not fixed. But the exemption is again a test on ability text (does the name begin with 'waaagh'). In the decoded bench saves, all 4 Stormboyz per Ork side also carry 'Full Throttle: The unit gains the Advance & Charge ability.' The engine never grants that (they are not SPEED FREEKS, and Kult of Speed advance_allows_charge covers SPEED FREEKS only). So the patch never fires on the bench analogue of s7468 and leaves that exact bug in every Ork bench game. It fires only on 2 Gretchin units and the Mek (0-2 per game), and never in the Custodes mirror, so the bench would measure noise. It has the same Keep Huntin'! regression in Orks_2000. verdict.reasons:
I checked these claims against 5e70bc2, the decoded bench saves and the finding saves.

All three designs find the same misread. _melee_chase_gate (L2641-2649) counts any ability text containing 'advance' and 'charge' as advance-and-charge, and with that flag it always Advances. ChargePhase (L2040) allows a charge after an Advance only through EffectPrimitivesData.has_effect_advance_and_charge. All three flip s7468 r3 P2 to a Normal-move attack, which is the measured mode (the Prosecutors are next to obj_nml_1). That position is a real lost charge: the Beast Snagga Boyz are dead and the Waaagh! is spent.

Why GAME wins:
- It uses the engine's own predicate at the one decision the evidence covers.
- It leaves AI-GAP-4 and RACE-1 alone, so no race-Advance guardrail can move. That includes harmful s7470, s7436, s7437 and s7438.
- At s7418 (holding is the measured-harmful alternative) it only changes the mode. 8.8" is less than M12, so the unit ends in the same place and can now charge. That is not a move toward holding.
- It fires in the bench rosters:
  - Ork side: 4 Stormboyz, 2 Gretchin and the Mek per side, outside the War Cry turn.
  - Custodes side: lone Blade Champions. Their 'Martial Inspiration' text matches, but CustodesAbilities grants advance-and-charge only with the Dropship flag.
  - Unchanged: SPEED FREEKS (Kult of Speed grant) and the Stompa (Waaagh! Effigy riles it permanently through _apply_permanent_states).

Why NARROW loses: its exemption is again ability text (the name must start with 'waaagh'). Bench Stormboyz also carry 'Full Throttle: The unit gains the Advance & Charge ability.', and the engine does not grant it. So narrow never fires on the bench analogue of the finding and leaves that exact bug in every Ork bench game. It changes only Gretchin and the Mek, so the bench would measure noise.

Why ROOT is second: it is the most general, but its RACE-1 change applies the M+12" 'keep the charge' check to every text-matched unit that has no grant. That includes Orks_2000 shooters (the s7436 cascade toward the neutral alternative that leans negative) and bench Gretchin hordes. These are unmeasured hold-backs of the kind that cost round 2 6.26 VP per game.

A defect all three share (reviewers' major issue, confirmed in the s7473 r3 save):
- The Beastboss is attached to 3 Beast Snagga Boyz, and ork11e_ab_uses.keep_huntin.round = 2 at the round-3 decision, so Keep Huntin'! is free that round.
- OrkAbilities11e offers it at unit_selected_to_move, the AI scores it 2.5 against a 1.0 bar, and rile_up_diffs sets effect_advance_and_charge.
- So the base Advances at s7473 and s7472 were legal. All three designs throw away legal approach there.
- s7473's +10.03 came from staying on obj_center. None of the designs fixes that; it stays open as a hold-versus-attack problem.

This defect is not in the bench rosters, but it ships to players, so the fix for it is required.

Custodes mirror: lone-Blade-Champion attack-Advances ('closing to charge range') occur about 0.67 times per game in the 6 V9-era records on disk. The older V0-V5 records show 5.63 per game over 224 games. So most Custodes-mirror pairs should stay identical. That fixture still has to be read separately.

The new static helper returns false unless GameConstants.edition >= 11. Then, with oa = _ork_abilities(), for each [slug, kw] in [["keep_huntin","BEAST SNAGGA"],["intimidating_motivation","ORKS"],["get_back_in_da_race","SPEED FREEKS"]], it returns true when oa.group_holder(unit_id, slug) != "" and oa.group_has_keyword(unit_id, kw) and not oa.army_used_this_round(player, slug). With ork11e_ab_uses.keep_huntin.round not equal to the current round, expect advance=true. With it equal to the current round, expect advance=false. Correct the report. s7473 and s7472 are Advances made legal by Keep Huntin'! (keep_huntin.round = 2 at the round-3 decision); after the first change they are unchanged. s7473's +10.03 comes from holding obj_center and stays open as a hold-versus-attack follow-up. s7468 is the only genuine lost charge. From root: put the decision in one helper, _unit_can_charge_after_advance(unit, unit_id, player) (flag OR engine predicate OR rile at selection; the old text test when the param is 0). If the charge_low_odds winner also merges, rerun the Stormboyz position with a 9-12" gap with both fixes on.
verdict.merge_risk:
Code risk is low.
- The patch is one guarded block in _melee_chase_gate plus a const. Reviewers checked that it applies to V9R with offsets only.
- It does not depend on FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE. The V9R kr_gate probe only checks whether the gate result is empty, and it is off in V9R.
- No other round-4 design edits the chase gate.
- Pass 2.5 still converts the same units to ATTACK; only the attack_advance mode changes.

Behaviour risks:
1. Without the first required change, every Orks_2000 Beast Snagga + Beastboss chase within 18" outside the War Cry turn gives up about 2" of legal approach. The charge chance drops from about 92% to 72% at 12", and from 58% to 28% at 15". The bench rosters have no holder of these abilities, so the bench cannot see this.
2. The Custodes-mirror Blade Champion flips are unmeasured (0.67 per game in V9-era records), in the fixture that punished round 2.
3. Gaps of 9-12" after the move give long-shot charges. If the charge is declined, the unit sits about 2" short. This gets worse if charge_low_odds lands.
4. The bench mostly measures frozen-roster Stormboyz, not the Orks_2000 positions where the finding was measured.
